# MPESB MP Police Constable Recruitment 2026: Comprehensive Guide

The Madhya Pradesh Employee Selection Board (MPESB) has officially released the much-awaited notification for the **MP Police Constable Recruitment 2026**. With an impressive offering of **7500 vacancies** for the General Duty (GD) Constable position, this recruitment drive is a golden opportunity for candidates aspiring to serve in the state police force. The online application process will commence on **22 September 2026** and will remain open until **06 October 2026**.

This comprehensive article delves deep into every aspect of the MP Police Constable Recruitment 2026. From intricate details about the job profile, salary breakdown, and career progression, to a meticulous analysis of the syllabus and previous year trends, we cover it all to ensure you are thoroughly prepared for the rigorous selection process.

---

## 1. Overview of the MP Police Constable Recruitment 2026

The MPESB conducts the MP Police Constable exam to select dynamic and physically fit individuals to maintain law and order across Madhya Pradesh. The 2026 recruitment aims to fill 7500 General Duty (GD) posts.

- **Conducting Body:** Madhya Pradesh Employee Selection Board (MPESB)
- **Post Name:** Police Constable (General Duty)
- **Total Vacancies:** 7500 Posts
- **Application Mode:** Online
- **Job Location:** Madhya Pradesh
- **Official Website:** esb.mp.gov.in

---

## 2. Important Dates and Schedule

Staying updated with the recruitment timeline is crucial to ensure you do not miss any critical deadlines. Below is the detailed schedule for the MP Police Constable Exam 2026:

- **Notification Release Date:** September 2026
- **Apply Online Start Date:** 22 September 2026
- **Apply Online Last Date:** 06 October 2026
- **Last Date for Fee Payment:** 06 October 2026
- **Last Date for Form Correction:** 11 October 2026
- **Examination Date:** 19 November 2026
- **Admit Card Release:** Before Exam (Dates to be updated)
- **Result Declaration:** To be updated soon

---

## 3. Total Vacancies Breakdown

The recruitment drive boasts a total of **7500 vacancies** for the post of Police Constable (General Duty). While the detailed category-wise (UR, SC, ST, OBC, EWS) breakdown is usually provided in the official detailed notification PDF, candidates can expect a fair distribution as per the state government's reservation policies. There are also specific quotas for female candidates and ex-servicemen.

---

## 4. Detailed Eligibility Criteria

To participate in the MP Police Constable Recruitment 2026, candidates must meet the stringent eligibility criteria set by the MPESB.

### Educational Qualification
For the General Duty (GD) Constable post, candidates generally need to have passed their **10th Class (High School)** or **12th Class (Intermediate)** from a recognized board. (Specifics vary slightly for reserved categories like ST, who might be eligible with an 8th pass, but 10th is the standard).

### Nationality
The candidate must be a citizen of India. Candidates from states other than Madhya Pradesh can also apply, but they will be considered under the Unreserved (UR) category regardless of their actual category.

---

## 5. Age Limit Requirements

The age criteria for the MP Police Constable recruitment as of the crucial date (**06 October 2026**) are as follows:

- **Minimum Age:** 18 Years
- **Maximum Age:** 33 Years

### Age Relaxation
Age relaxation is applicable as per the Madhya Pradesh government rules for reserved categories (SC/ST/OBC) and female candidates, generally extending the upper age limit by 5 years (making it up to 38 years).

---

## 6. Application Fee Details

The application fee varies based on the category of the applicant and the type of recruitment (direct or departmental). 

- **For UR Candidates:** ₹ 500/-
- **For SC, ST, OBC, EWS Candidates (MP Domicile):** ₹ 250/-

**Exam Fee for Departmental Recruitment:**
- **For UR Candidates:** ₹ 200/-
- **For SC, ST, OBC, EWS Candidates:** ₹ 100/-

*Note: Portal charges will be levied extra on top of the examination fee.*

### Payment Mode
Payment can be made online via:
- Debit Card
- Credit Card
- Internet Banking
- IMPS
- Cash Card / Mobile Wallets (like Paytm, PhonePe, etc.)

---

## 7. How to Apply Online

Follow these step-by-step instructions to successfully submit your application for the MP Police Constable Recruitment 2026:

1. **Visit the Official Website:** Go to the MPESB official portal at esb.mp.gov.in.
2. **Profile Registration:** First-time users must create a profile on the MPOnline portal, generating a registration number and password.
3. **Login:** Use your credentials to log in and search for the "MP Police Constable Recruitment 2026" link.
4. **Fill the Details:** Accurately fill out personal, educational, and communication details.
5. **Upload Documents:** Upload scanned copies of a recent passport-sized photograph, signature, and necessary certificates in the prescribed format.
6. **Pay the Fee:** Proceed to the payment gateway and pay the requisite application fee online.
7. **Submit and Print:** Submit the application form and take a printout of the final confirmation page for future reference.

---

## 8. Detailed Job Profile & Responsibilities (Day-to-day work)

Being a Police Constable in Madhya Pradesh is a demanding yet highly respected job. A constable forms the backbone of the police force and is the first point of contact for the public.

**Day-to-Day Responsibilities:**
- **Patrolling:** Regular patrolling in assigned beats (areas) to prevent crimes and ensure public safety.
- **FIR and Documentation:** Assisting Head Constables and Sub-Inspectors in writing FIRs (First Information Reports), maintaining station diaries, and handling paperwork.
- **Law and Order Maintenance:** Managing crowds during festivals, rallies, VIP visits, or protests.
- **Investigation Assistance:** Helping senior officers in crime investigations by protecting crime scenes, gathering basic evidence, and recording statements of witnesses.
- **Traffic Management:** Occasionally, GD constables may be deployed to manage traffic at busy intersections.
- **Community Policing:** Engaging with the local community to build trust, resolve minor disputes, and gather local intelligence.

---

## 9. Comprehensive Salary Breakdown & Allowances

A career in the MP Police offers excellent financial stability along with state government benefits. The salary structure is based on the 7th Pay Commission.

- **Pay Scale:** ₹19,500 - ₹62,000/- (Pay Level 4)
- **Basic Pay:** ₹19,500/-

**Allowances and Perks:**
- **Dearness Allowance (DA):** A significant percentage of the basic pay, revised bi-annually to adjust for inflation.
- **House Rent Allowance (HRA):** Provided if government quarters are not allotted. It varies based on the posting location (urban vs. rural).
- **Travel Allowance (TA):** To cover daily commuting and travel for official duties.
- **Uniform Allowance:** Provided annually for the maintenance of the police uniform.
- **Medical Allowances:** Comprehensive health coverage for the constable and their dependents.
- **Pension:** Covered under the National Pension System (NPS).

The gross initial in-hand salary typically ranges between **₹24,000 to ₹27,000/-** per month, depending on the posting location and current DA rates.

---

## 10. Career Growth & Promotions Hierarchy

The MP Police department offers a well-defined career progression path for Constables who demonstrate dedication, discipline, and aptitude. Promotions are based on a mix of seniority, performance records, and departmental examinations.

**The Hierarchy:**
1. **Police Constable (PC):** The entry-level post.
2. **Head Constable (HC):** The first promotion, usually achieved after 8-12 years of service or by clearing internal departmental exams.
3. **Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI):** With further experience and clearing promotional tests, one can become an ASI, marked by one star on the uniform.
4. **Sub-Inspector (SI):** A highly respected field officer post, marked by two stars.
5. **Inspector (TI/SHO):** Exceptional candidates can retire as an Inspector, heading a police station.

---

## 11. Selection Process

The selection for MP Police Constable involves multiple rigorous stages to ensure only the best candidates are chosen.

1. **Written Examination (CBT):** A Computer Based Test evaluating knowledge across various subjects.
2. **Physical Efficiency Test (PET):** Tests of physical endurance like running, long jump, and shot put.
3. **Physical Standard Test (PST):** Measurement of height and chest (for males) to ensure they meet the minimum standards.
4. **Medical Examination:** A thorough medical check-up including eyesight and overall fitness.
5. **Document Verification:** Final verification of all educational and identity documents.

---

## 12. Physical Standard Test (PST) Details

Candidates must meet the following minimum physical standards to qualify:

**For Male Candidates (UR/OBC/SC):**
- **Height:** 168 cm
- **Chest:** 81 cm (Unexpanded) and 86 cm (Expanded)

**For Male Candidates (ST):**
- **Height:** 160 cm
- **Chest:** 76 cm (Unexpanded) and 81 cm (Expanded)

**For Female Candidates (All Categories):**
- **Height:** 155 cm
- **Chest:** Not Applicable

---

## 13. Physical Efficiency Test (PET) Criteria

The PET assesses the stamina and athletic ability of the candidates. The standards typically include:

- **800 Meters Race:** Must be completed within a specific time (e.g., 2 minutes 45 seconds for males; 4 minutes for females).
- **Long Jump:** A minimum distance (e.g., 13 feet for males, 10 feet for females).
- **Shot Put:** Throwing a heavy sphere (usually 7.26 kg for males, 4 kg for females) up to a designated distance.

*Note: Marks for PET have been introduced in recent years, making physical fitness equally as important as the written exam.*

---

## 14. Exam Pattern

The written examination is an objective type Computer Based Test (CBT). 

- **Total Questions:** 100
- **Total Marks:** 100
- **Duration:** 2 Hours (120 minutes)
- **Marking Scheme:** 1 mark is awarded for every correct answer. There is generally **no negative marking** in the MP Police Constable exam.
- **Language:** Bilingual (English and Hindi)

**Sections:**
1. General Knowledge & Logical Knowledge - 40 Marks
2. Intellectual Ability & Mental Aptitude - 30 Marks
3. Science & Simple Arithmetic - 30 Marks

---

## 15. In-depth Syllabus Analysis (Subject by subject breakdown)

Understanding the syllabus is the first step toward effective preparation.

### General Knowledge & Logical Knowledge (40 Marks)
- **MP G.K.:** History, Geography, Culture, Economy, and Polity of Madhya Pradesh. (Highly crucial).
- **Indian History & Geography:** Focus on the modern Indian independence movement and basic physical geography.
- **Current Affairs:** National and international events, sports, awards, and important dates from the last 6-8 months.
- **Indian Constitution:** Basic articles, fundamental rights, and the structure of the government.

### Intellectual Ability & Mental Aptitude (30 Marks)
- **Verbal & Non-Verbal Reasoning:** Analogies, similarities, differences, space visualization, spatial orientation, problem-solving, analysis, judgment, decision making, visual memory.
- **Aptitude:** Coding and decoding, statement conclusion, syllogistic reasoning, blood relations, and direction sense.

### Science & Simple Arithmetic (30 Marks)
- **General Science:** Physics, Chemistry, and Biology of the 10th standard level. Focus on everyday science, human body diseases, and basic chemical reactions.
- **Arithmetic:** Number systems, simplification, decimals, fractions, LCM, HCF, ratio and proportion, percentage, average, profit and loss, discount, simple and compound interest, mensuration, time and work, time and distance.

---

## 16. Preparation Strategy

To crack the MP Police Constable Exam 2026, a structured preparation strategy is imperative.

- **Master the Syllabus:** Break down the syllabus and allocate specific days to each topic. Do not ignore MP General Knowledge, as it carries heavy weightage.
- **Daily Time Table:** Dedicate at least 6-8 hours daily. Allocate 2 hours for Mathematics, 2 for Reasoning, 2 for G.K./Science, and 2 for physical training.
- **Physical Fitness:** Do not wait for the written exam results to start physical training. Run daily, practice long jumps, and build stamina from day one.
- **Mock Tests:** Take full-length mock tests every weekend to build time management skills. Analyze your mistakes and work on weak areas.
- **Revision:** Consistent revision is key. Make short notes for formulas in math and important dates/facts in G.K.

---

## 17. Recommended Books

Investing in the right study material can make a huge difference:

- **MP G.K.:** 'Madhya Pradesh Ek Parichay' by McGraw Hill or Mukesh Maheshwari's MP G.K. book.
- **Mathematics:** 'Quantitative Aptitude' by R.S. Aggarwal.
- **Reasoning:** 'A Modern Approach to Verbal & Non-Verbal Reasoning' by R.S. Aggarwal.
- **General Science:** Lucent's General Science.
- **General Knowledge:** Lucent's General Knowledge (for History, Polity, and Geography).
- **Practice Sets:** Arihant or Kiran Publications' MP Police Constable Previous Year Solved Papers.

---

## 18. Previous Year Cut-off Trends & Exam Difficulty

The cut-off for the MP Police Constable exam depends on the number of vacancies, the difficulty level of the paper, and the number of candidates.

Historically, the paper ranges from **Easy to Moderate** in difficulty. The arithmetic is basic, but the reasoning and MP G.K. questions can be tricky.

**Expected Safe Score (Out of 100 for Written Exam):**
- **UR (Male):** 75 - 80
- **OBC (Male):** 72 - 77
- **SC (Male):** 65 - 70
- **ST (Male):** 60 - 65
- **Female Candidates:** Generally 8-10 marks lower than their respective male category cut-offs.

*Aiming for a score above 80 is advisable to ensure a secure spot in the final merit list, considering the high competition.*

---

## 19. Admit Card Information

The MPESB will release the admit card for the written examination typically 7-10 days before the exam date (19 November 2026). Candidates must download the admit card from the official website using their application number and date of birth. 

The admit card will contain crucial details such as the exam center address, reporting time, and specific guidelines for exam day. A hard copy of the admit card, along with an original valid Photo ID (Aadhar Card, Voter ID, etc.), is mandatory for entry into the examination hall.

---

## 20. Answer Key and Objection Management

A few days after the completion of the CBT, the MPESB will publish a provisional answer key. Candidates will have the opportunity to cross-check their answers and calculate their tentative scores. 

If a candidate finds any discrepancies in the provisional answer key, they can raise objections online by paying a nominal fee per question. After reviewing all objections, a final answer key will be released, based on which the final results will be calculated.

---

## 21. Result and Merit List

The MP Police Constable result will be declared in stages. The first result will list candidates qualified for the Physical Efficiency Test (PET) and Physical Standard Test (PST). 

After the physical tests, a final merit list will be prepared. This final list will take into account the combined scores of the written examination and the physical tests (as per the latest recruitment rules). The final merit list will be category-wise and will determine the ultimate selection for the 7500 posts.

---

## 22. Important Links

Keep these links handy for quick access to official updates and application portals:

- **Official Notification PDF:** [Click Here (Link to be updated)]
- **Apply Online Link:** [Click Here (Link to be active on 22 Sept 2026)]
- **Download Admit Card:** [Click Here (Link to be updated)]
- **Official Website:** [esb.mp.gov.in](https://esb.mp.gov.in/e_default.html)
- **SarkariResult Latest Jobs:** [Click Here](https://sarkariresult.com.cm/latest-jobs/)

Ensure you complete your application process well before the deadline of **06 October 2026** to avoid last-minute server issues. Start your preparation earnestly to secure your place in the prestigious Madhya Pradesh Police Force!
